sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Mughal Empire** (मुगल साम्राज्य), a powerful imperial power in the Indian subcontinent.
Established in **1526** by **Babur** and lasted effectively until **1707** (Great Mughals), with decline continuing till **1857**.
Spanned across large parts of **India**, **Pakistan**, **Bangladesh**, and eastern **Afghanistan**.
Founded by **Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur**, descending from **Timur** (paternal side) and **Genghis Khan** (maternal side).
Unified most of the Indian subcontinent under a single centralized administration, revolutionized revenue systems (**Zahb / Zabti**), and left a rich legacy of art, architecture, and literature.
**Mansabdari System**, **Zabti Revenue System**, religious policies (**Din-i-Ilahi**, **Jizya** abolition by Akbar, reimposition by Aurangzeb), and monumental architecture.
High-scoring segment in Indian History; questions frequently appear on **Battles of Panipat**, **Akbar's Navratnas**, architectural sites, and revenue terms.
Official language was **Persian**; capital shifted multiple times between **Agra**, **Delhi**, **Lahore**, and **Fatehpur Sikri**.

items.title: Foundation and Early Rulers (Babur & Humayun)
items.content:
• **Babur** defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** in the **First Battle of Panipat** (**1526**) to establish the empire.
• Wrote his autobiography **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** (Baburnama) in **Turkic**.
• **Humayun** lost the empire to **Sher Shah Suri** after the **Battle of Chausa** (**1539**) and **Battle of Kannauj** (**1540**).
• Regained Delhi throne in **1555** with help of Persian ruler **Shah Tahmasp**.
• **Mnemonic for Chronology of Early Mughals:** **BHAJ** (**B**abur, **H**umayun, **A**kbar, **J**ahangir).

items.title: Golden Age under Akbar and Jahangir
items.content:
• **Akbar** ascended throne at age 13 under **Bairam Khan** (**1556**).
• Won **Second Battle of Panipat** (**1556**) against **Hemu**.
• Abolished **Jizya** (**1564**) and pilgrimage tax; introduced **Sulh-i-Kul** (peace with all) and **Din-i-Ilahi** (**1582**).
• **Jahangir** focused on justice (**Zanjir-i-Adl** or chain of justice) and patronized painting.
• **Nur Jahan** (wife) exercised de facto power during Jahangir's reign.

items.title: Peak of Architecture and Decline (Shah Jahan & Aurangzeb)
items.content:
• **Shah Jahan**'s reign is known as the **Golden Age of Mughal Architecture** (**Taj Mahal**, **Red Fort**, **Jama Masjid**).
• **Aurangzeb** (Alamgir) expanded the empire to its greatest territorial extent.
• Re-imposed **Jizya** (**1679**), executed **Guru Tegh Bahadur** (9th Sikh Guru), and reversed liberal policies.
• Led to massive rebellions by **Marathas** (**Shivaji**), **Sikhs**, and **Rajputs**, leading to empire's downfall.
• **Mnemonic for Great 6 Mughals:** **B-H-A-J-S-A** (**B**abur, **H**umayun, **A**kbar, **J**ahangir, **S**hah Jahan, **A**urangzeb).

items.title: Mughal Administration and Revenue Systems
items.content:
• **Mansabdari System:** Introduced by **Akbar**, graded civil and military officials (**Zat** for rank, **Sawar** for cavalry).
• **Zabti / Dahsala System:** Revenue system managed by **Todar Mal** (Akbar's revenue minister), fixing tax based on 10-year average yield.
• **Central Administration:** **Wakil** (Prime minister), **Diwan** (Revenue head), **Mir Bakshi** (Military head & intelligence), **Sadr-us-Sudur** (Ecclesiastical & grants head).
• Provincial administration divided into **Subas** (governed by **Subedar**), **Sarkars**, and **Parganas**.

items.title: Art, Culture, and Literature
items.content:
• **Painting:** Reached pinnacle under **Jahangir** (masters like **Ustad Mansur** and **Abul Hasan**).
• **Literature:** **Ain-i-Akbari** and **Akbarnama** written by **Abul Fazl** in Persian; **Padshahnama** by **Abdul Hamid Lahori**.
• **Translation Bureau (Maktab Khana):** Sanskrit works like **Mahabharata** translated into Persian as **Razmnama**.
• **Architecture Style:** Use of **Pietra Dura** (inlay work with semi-precious stones), **Charbagh** garden layout, and marble domes.

items.term: Trick 1: Sequence of Great Mughal Emperors
items.definition: Use the acronym **B-H-A-J-S-A** (Bhajsa) -> **B**abur, **H**umayun, **A**kbar, **J**ahangir, **S**hah Jahan, **A**urangzeb.
Use the sentence: '**P**anipar mein **K**hana khaya, **Ch**anderi gaya, **G**haghra pehna' -> **P**anipat (1526), **K**hanwa (1527), **Ch**anderi (1528), **G**haghra (1529).

Use the mnemonic **ATM FOR BBN** -> **A**bul Fazl, **T**odar Mal, **M**ansi Singh, **F**aizi, **O**mar Khan (Tansen), **R**ahim Khan-i-Khana, **B**irbal, **B**allabhacharya / Mulla Do-Piyaza, **N**aksh Hakim.

items.term: Trick 4: Major Monuments Built by Shah Jahan
items.definition: Use the word **MAT JAHAN** -> **M**otimashjid, **A**gra Fort additions, **T**aj Mahal, **J**ama Masjid, **A**gra Gardens, **H**umayun adjustments (Red Fort / Shahjahanabad).
Remember **Baburnama** was written in **Turkic** (Chagatai Turkic), NOT Persian, even though Persian was the court language of later Mughals.
Remember **Zat** = Personal rank/salary grade; **Sawar** = Number of horsemen/cavalry maintained.
Students confuse **1526** (Panipat), **1527** (Khanwa), **1528** (Chanderi), and **1529** (Ghaghra). Remember they happen in consecutive years immediately after Babur entered India.

items.term: Mistake 2: Who built Taj Mahal vs Red Fort
items.definition: Both were built by **Shah Jahan**, NOT Akbar or Aurangzeb. Akbar built Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.
Students often assume court language **Persian** was used by Babur. Babur wrote in **Turkic** (Chagatai); it was translated into Persian later by **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana**.

items.term: Mistake 4: Jizya Tax Abolition and Re-imposition
items.definition: **Akbar abolished** Jizya in **1564**, but **Aurangzeb re-imposed** it in **1679**. Do not mix up the two emperors.
Humayun did NOT rule continuously from 1530 to 1556. He lost power to **Sher Shah Suri** from **1540 to 1555** during his exile.
Battle of Haldighati (**1576**) was fought between **Akbar's army (led by Man Singh)** and **Maharana Pratap**, NOT Akbar in person.
**Babur** defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** in the **First Battle of Panipat** to found the Mughal Empire.
**Sher Shah Suri** defeated Humayun and introduced administrative reforms like the **Grand Trunk Road** and **Rupiah**.
Akbar consolidated empire through matrimonial alliances, **Mansabdari system**, **Zabti revenue system**, and religious tolerance (**Din-i-Ilahi**).
Noted for patronage of **Mughal painting**, justice chain (**Zanjir-i-Adl**), and influence of **Nur Jahan**.
Period of grand architecture including the **Taj Mahal**, **Red Fort**, and **Jama Masjid** in white marble.
Achieved maximum territorial limits but alienated Rajputs, Sikhs, and Marathas due to religious orthodoxy and re-imposition of **Jizya**.
**Persian** was the official administrative and court language of the Mughal Empire.
**Diwan** (finance/revenue) and **Mir Bakshi** (military) were key pillars of central administration.
Akbar's court featured nine luminaries including **Birbal**, **Tansen**, **Todar Mal**, and **Abul Fazl**.
The empire disintegrated rapidly after Aurangzeb's death in **1707**, paving the way for regional kingdoms and British colonial dominance.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on match-the-following questions regarding Mughal monuments, their builders, and the years of major battles like Panipat (1526, 1556).
Memorize Akbar's administrative terms like Zabti, Dahsala, Mansab, Zat, and Sawar as vocabulary-based questions frequently appear.
UPSSSC often tests whether Baburnama was written in Persian or Turkic. Remember: Babur wrote in Turkic, but Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana translated it into Persian.
Do not confuse Sher Shah Suri's reign duration (1540–1545) with the entire Sur dynasty interregnum (1540–1555) leading up to Humayun's restoration.

keyTakeaways: Mughal Empire was founded in **1526** by **Babur** after defeating **Ibrahim Lodi** at Panipat.
**Akbar** laid the robust administrative foundation via **Mansabdari** and **Zabti** systems.
**Shah Jahan**'s era represents the architectural peak (**Taj Mahal**, **Red Fort**).
**Aurangzeb** expanded the empire to its maximum extent but sowed seeds of decline through religious policies.
Major battles to remember: Panipat (1526, 1556), Khanwa (1527), Chausa (1539), Kannauj (1540), Haldighati (1576).
